headline: Local Man Expresses Relief After FBI Adds His Name To 'Most Wanted' List, Solving His Existential Boredom
body:
Q: Mr. Sharma, you were recently declared a person of interest by the FBI for an alleged international financial scheme. How do you feel?

A: Honestly? Relieved. For years, I’ve been living in a suburb in New Jersey, waking up at 7:00 AM to answer emails about supply chain logistics. I was essentially a ghost in the system. Getting on a high-stakes, international wanted list gave me the kind of recognition I hadn't felt since winning the regional spelling bee in 1998.

Q: The authorities allege you managed to siphon millions through a series of shell companies. Do you have a comment?

A: People focus on the ‘siphoning’ part, but they don’t understand the administrative burden of running eighteen companies out of a one-bedroom apartment. I’ve been spending my afternoons curating a portfolio of luxury assets, which is far more fulfilling than my previous career in data entry. It’s not about the fraud; it’s about finally being a character in a spy novel instead of the background extra.

Q: Do you plan to surrender to the authorities to resolve these federal charges?

A: Why would I do that? I’ve finally started receiving high-quality mail, and I’m currently on a waitlist for a private bunker in the hills. If I turn myself in, I go back to being someone who has to wait in line at the DMV. Right now, I’m an international fugitive. The service is significantly better.
caption: Living your best life is all about finding a career path that keeps the federal authorities interested in your daily itinerary. #FBI #LifeGoals #FugitiveLifestyle #WantedMan (satire)
